breakfast.name: Burek (Phyllo Meat Pie)
ingredients: Filling: 500g ground beef and pork, 1 onion, salt, pepper
instructions: Sauté onion, add ground meat, cook until browned, season
Roll phyllo sheets thin, brush with oil
Place filling along the edge, roll into a log
Coil the log into a spiral in a round baking pan
Brush top with oil
Bake at 180°C for 35-40 min until golden and flaky
Serve with cold yogurt
breakfast.description: Spiral phyllo pie with meat — eaten for breakfast at bakeries across Croatia. The burek is ordered by filling: meat (burek), cheese (sirnica), spinach (zeljanica).

breakfast.name: Palačinke (Thin Pancakes)
ingredients: Nutella, jam, or walnuts with sugar for filling
instructions: Whisk eggs, flour, milk, salt into thin batter
Heat buttered pan, pour thin layer
Cook until bottom is golden, flip
Spread with Nutella, jam, or crushed walnuts mixed with sugar
Roll up
Dust with powdered sugar
breakfast.description: Croatian crêpes — thinner and softer than American pancakes. The walnut-sugar filling is the traditional Dalmatian version.

breakfast.name: Štrukli (Cottage Cheese Rolls)
ingredients: Dough: 300g flour, 1 egg, 2 tbsp oil, warm water, salt
Filling: 500g fresh cottage cheese (svježi sir), 2 eggs, sour cream, salt
instructions: Make dough, rest 30 min
Stretch dough thin on floured cloth (like strudel)
Mix cottage cheese, eggs, sour cream, salt
Spread filling over stretched dough
Roll up using the cloth to help
Cut into portions
Place in buttered baking dish, top with sour cream
Bake at 180°C for 25-30 min until golden and bubbly
breakfast.description: Cottage cheese-filled rolled pastry — the pride of Zagreb's Zagorje region. Baked (zapečeni) is the classic way, boiled (kuhani) is the lighter version.

lunch.name: Peka (Under-the-Bell Roast)
instructions: Cut meat or octopus into pieces
Toss with vegetables, garlic, rosemary, oil, wine
Place in a round baking dish
Cover with peka bell (cast iron dome)
Pile hot coals on top and around the bell
Cook 90-120 min without opening
Everything steams and roasts simultaneously under the bell — the lid traps all the moisture
lunch.description: Meat and vegetables roasted under a cast-iron bell covered with embers — Dalmatia's most ancient and celebrated cooking method. You don't check it; you trust it.

lunch.name: Pasticada (Dalmatian Braised Beef)
instructions: Lard beef with strips of prosciutto using a larding needle
Marinate overnight in wine, vinegar, and aromatics
Brown beef on all sides in hot oil
Add chopped vegetables, cook until soft
Add marinade, tomato paste, prunes, cloves, bay leaf
Braise covered on low for 3 hours until fork-tender
Remove meat, blend sauce until smooth
Slice beef, serve with the rich dark sauce over gnocchi
lunch.description: Dalmatia's wedding dish — beef larded with prosciutto, braised for hours in red wine with prunes. The sauce is blended smooth and poured over gnocchi. Reserved for the most important occasions.

lunch.name: Crni Rižot (Black Risotto)
ingredients: 500g cuttlefish or squid (cleaned, ink sacs reserved)
instructions: Sauté onion and garlic in olive oil
Add sliced cuttlefish, cook until white
Add rice, toast 2 min
Add wine, stir until absorbed
Add fish stock one ladle at a time, stirring constantly
Halfway through, add reserved ink — the risotto turns jet black
Continue adding stock until rice is al dente and creamy
Finish with olive oil, parsley
Serve — the dramatic black color is the point
lunch.description: Jet-black cuttlefish risotto — the ink turns everything midnight dark. A Dalmatian coast showstopper that stains your lips for hours.

dinner.name: Ćevapi with Lepinja
instructions: Mix meat with grated onion, garlic, baking soda, salt, pepper
Refrigerate 2+ hours
Shape into small finger-sized links
Grill over charcoal, turning once
Serve in split lepinja bread with diced raw onion, ajvar, and kajmak
dinner.description: Grilled meat fingers in flatbread — the Balkans' universal street food. Croatian ćevapi are smaller and the bread (lepinja) is round and pillowy.

dinner.name: Brodetto (Fish Stew)
ingredients: Mixed fish: scorpionfish, monkfish, mullet, shrimp
instructions: Sauté onions and garlic in olive oil
Add tomatoes, wine, vinegar, bay leaf
Simmer 10 min
Add firmest fish first, delicate fish and shrimp later
Cook gently 15-20 min — do not stir, only shake the pot
The fish should hold its shape in the rich tomato broth
Serve over polenta with parsley
dinner.description: Adriatic fishermen's stew — each coastal town claims the original recipe. The rule: never stir, only shake the pot, so the fish stays whole.

dinner.name: Janjetina s Ražnja (Spit-Roasted Lamb)
instructions: Clean and prepare lamb
Rub with salt, garlic, rosemary, olive oil
Mount on spit over charcoal pit
Roast slowly, turning continuously, for 3+ hours
Baste with drippings — the skin should be crispy, the meat falling off the bone
Carve and serve with roasted potatoes and salad
dinner.description: Whole lamb on a spit — the centerpiece of every Dalmatian celebration. The slow rotation over coals takes patience, and the result is worth every hour.

snacks.name: Fritule (Croatian Doughnuts)
instructions: Mix flour, yeast, sugar, eggs, milk, salt, citrus zest, rum
Fold in raisins
Let rise 1 hour
Drop spoonfuls into hot oil — they puff up
Fry until golden all around
Dust heavily with powdered sugar
snacks.description: Tiny citrus-scented doughnut balls — the smell of Croatian Christmas. Sold by the dozen at every Advent market.

snacks.name: Soparnik (Swiss Chard Pie)
ingredients: Dough: flour, water, olive oil, salt
Filling: Swiss chard (chopped), garlic, parsley, olive oil
instructions: Make thin dough, divide in two
Roll first half paper-thin
Spread with raw chopped chard, garlic, parsley
Cover with second paper-thin dough layer
Bake on hot stone or in very hot oven until crispy
Brush with olive oil
Cut into diamonds
snacks.description: Paper-thin double-crusted chard pie from Poljica — UNESCO intangible heritage. Traditionally baked on a stone under a peka bell.

desserts.name: Kremšnita (Custard Cream Slice)
ingredients: Custard: 6 egg yolks, 150g sugar, 50g cornstarch, 750ml milk, vanilla
Whipped cream: 500ml heavy cream, 2 tbsp sugar
instructions: Bake puff pastry sheets at 200°C until golden and puffed
Make custard: whisk yolks, sugar, cornstarch, temper with hot milk, cook until thick
Cool custard completely
Whip cream to stiff peaks
Place one pastry sheet in pan
Spread custard layer, then whipped cream layer
Top with second pastry sheet
Dust with powdered sugar
Chill, cut into squares
desserts.description: Samobor's famous custard slice — two layers of puff pastry sandwiching custard and whipped cream. Every cafe in the town of Samobor claims the best.

desserts.name: Rožata (Dubrovnik Crème Caramel)
ingredients: Custard: 6 eggs, 150g sugar, 750ml milk, 1 tbsp rose liqueur (ružica), lemon zest, vanilla
instructions: Caramelize sugar in ramekins
Heat milk with lemon zest and vanilla
Whisk eggs with sugar
Temper with hot milk, add rose liqueur
Strain into caramelized ramekins
Bake in water bath at 160°C for 40-45 min
Chill overnight, unmold
desserts.description: Dubrovnik's crème caramel — perfumed with rose liqueur. A Renaissance-era dessert from the Republic of Ragusa.

desserts.name: Strukli (Baked Cheese Rolls)
ingredients: Dough: 300g flour, 1 egg, 2 tbsp oil, warm water, salt
Filling: 500g fresh cow's cheese (quark/farmer's cheese), 200g sour cream, 2 eggs, salt
instructions: Make dough, knead until smooth, rest 30 min under warm bowl
Stretch dough on a floured tablecloth until paper-thin — you should see through it
Spread cheese filling over the entire surface
Roll up using the tablecloth to help — like a strudel
Cut into individual rolls about 8cm wide
Place rolls in buttered baking dish
Pour sour cream and melted butter over the top
Bake at 180°C for 25-30 min until golden and bubbling
The cheese should be creamy inside, the top golden and slightly crispy
desserts.description: Zagreb's beloved baked cheese rolls — paper-thin stretched dough filled with fresh cheese and sour cream, baked until golden and bubbling. The dough-stretching technique (over a tablecloth, until you can read a newspaper through it) went viral as a showcase of Croatian grandmother cooking skills.

drinks.name: Gemišt (White Wine Spritzer)
instructions: Fill glass half with cold white wine
Top with cold sparkling water
Stir once
Drink in the sun
drinks.description: Half wine, half sparkling water — Croatia's summer drink. The Graševina grape from Slavonia is the traditional choice.

drinks.name: Rakija (Fruit Brandy)
ingredients: Fruit: plums (šljivovica), grapes (lozovača), pears (kruškovac), or herbs (travarica)
instructions: Ferment fruit with sugar and water for weeks
Distill in copper still
Collect middle cut (the heart) — discard heads and tails
Age in glass or oak
Serve at room temperature in small glasses
drinks.description: Croatian fruit brandy — every family makes their own from whatever fruit grows in the garden. Offered to every guest as an act of hospitality; refusing is rude.
